subject: Fwd: Problems with the app usage data source
body:
Dear Stefan,

I hope you are doing well, and I apologize for the delayed response.

The Android App Usage API monitors app activity, including the usage of specific packages (apps). The "start time" reflects when the API begins tracking an app’s usage, while the "end time" indicates when the observation period ends. These timestamps are automatically generated by the API's internal tracking mechanisms.

The "record time" refers to when Avicenna’s data collection cycle captures this data, which occurs every 5 minutes. The end time you’re seeing is provided by the Android App Usage API and may slightly differ from the record time due to differences between how the API tracks app usage and how our system captures and logs the data.

For example, in the highlighted rows, we observe app usage across three instances. In the first row, at the record time, we collected data, and the API provided the foreground time (fg_time) within the start_time and end_time window, along with the last_used value. In the next row, the end_time changed because we recorded data at the next cycle, and the API updated the fg_time and last_used values accordingly. To accurately analyze app usage, you will need to process this raw data by aligning the same start_times with the corresponding end_times to calculate the total fg_time.

Please feel free to reach out if you have any further questions.

Best regards,
Omid

we urgently need your support in interpreting the app usage data again. We are still unsure how to handle these "duplicate" entries to calculate the actual fg_time_ms.

(pasted image, please look explicitly at the entries marked in blue and those marked in light orange and check the consistency of the content)
What is meant with "calculating the total fg_time" (from your last response). To be able to calculate the actual fg_time, we would need to know if the fg_time is shared across duplicates (e.g. the blue highlited lines) - meaning the fg_time from line 17 is already included in the fg_time from line 16. Or is the fg_time of each line independant from other lines within the duplicates (meaning: 6461ms (from line 16) does not include the 3163ms (from line 17) and therefore all fg_time data have to be summed up for each block of duplicates.
Either way, the data does not add up: For the first way (fg_time is shared across duplicates), the fg_time of each consecutive line should not be able to get smaller - but it does bewteen line 16 and 17. The other way (fg_time needs to be summed up beacuse the data is independent of each other) would mean that the fg_time can't be greater than the length of the time window (start_time to end_time) - which is the case in line 32 (360 seconds is the time between end_time of previous line and end_time of line 32 while the fg_time is ~388 seconds).
For our calculations, we therefore urgently need an explanation in order to know how high the actual usage of an app (i.e. the fg_time) is within a very specific period of time.
You are welcome to calculate for us how long the fg_time is in total:
- 1) in the blue area between lines 16-17;
- 2) in the orange area between lines
29-30.
We also have another question regarding the last used variable: Is the time in last_used the last moment when the app in the foreground for the last time of the observation period? If so, how is it possible that lines 16 and 17 have the same last_used (which is the end of end_time from line 16) but the fg_time differs between both lines. If the app was last used at 09:52:00 - how is it possible that there are 3163 ms of fg_time 09:52:00 and 09:52:45?
Since record_time is just the timestemp for the aggregation of the variables by Avicenna, are we right to assue that it does not influence any researchquestion related questions, since what we are interested in are the variables tracked by the API (start_time, end_time, fg_time and last_used)?
Since clarifying these questions via email is difficult, we would greatly appreciate a short live meeting (e.g. via Zoom) to discuss the issue directly.
Please let us know if such a meeting is possible and when it would be convenient for you.
Thank you for your support!

Dear Stefan,
I hope you are doing well, and I apologize for the delayed response.
The Android App Usage API monitors app activity, including the usage of specific packages (apps). The "start time" reflects when the API begins tracking an app’s usage, while the "end time" indicates when the observation period ends. These timestamps are automatically generated by the API's internal tracking mechanisms.
The "record time" refers to when Avicenna’s data collection cycle captures this data, which occurs every 5 minutes. The end time you’re seeing is provided by the Android App Usage API and may slightly differ from the record time due to differences between how the API tracks app usage and how our system captures and logs the data.
For example, in the highlighted rows, we observe app usage across three instances. In the first row, at the record time, we collected data, and the API provided the foreground time (fg_time) within the start_time and end_time window, along with the last_used value. In the next row, the end_time changed because we recorded data at the next cycle, and the API updated the fg_time and last_used values accordingly. To accurately analyze app usage, you will need to process this raw data by aligning the same start_times with the corresponding end_times to calculate the total fg_time.
Please feel free to reach out if you have any further questions.
Best regards,
Omid

The Android App Usage API monitors app activity, including the usage of specific packages (apps). The "start time" reflects when the API begins tracking an app’s usage, while the "end time" indicates when the observation period ends. These timestamps are automatically generated by the API's internal tracking mechanisms.

The end time you’re seeing is provided by the Android App Usage API and may slightly differ from the record time due to differences between how the API tracks app usage and how our system captures and logs the data.

In the next row, the end_time changed because we recorded data at the next cycle, and the API updated the fg_time and last_used values accordingly. To accurately analyze app usage, you will need to process this raw data by aligning the same start_times with the corresponding end_times to calculate the total fg_time.
